name: BT Accounts
changelog:
0.6.0

  • Order notifications. A submitted order now emails the shop the moment it lands, with the whole order in the body — account, PO, end customer, piece count, in-hands date, every line with its size breakdown, and links to each art file.
  • The person who submitted it gets a branded receipt with the same copy, so there is no question about what they sent.
  • Optional status email: switch it on and the account is told every time the job card moves.
  • Set the notification address, the From address, and both toggles under BT Accounts → Order notifications, with a Send a test email button to prove SMTP before a real order arrives.
  • Printable work order. Every order now has a clean one-page sheet at /accounts/order/{id}/print — letterhead, account and PO, blanks inbound, ship-to, an items table with the size run called out per line, art thumbnails, notes, and sign-off lines for art, production and shipping.
  • Linked from Print order on the order page, a Print link on every row of the orders list, and Print work order in the shop queue — where it doubles as the pull ticket.
  • Prints letter portrait with the toolbar suppressed, so Save as PDF gives a clean sheet.

0.5.0

  • The Quote tab is live. Print or embroidery, locations or embroidery type, any quantity, with a live per-piece and total plus the full quantity-break table.
  • Always priced as customer-supplied — decoration only, no garment cost — using this account's rates.
  • Embroidery over 84 pieces still says contact us, exactly as the public quoter does.
  • Print now defaults instead of embroidery on the order form.

0.4.0

  • Order entry is live. The New Order tab now works: end customer, your PO, the blanks supplier and their PO, expected arrival, ship-to, in-hands date, and any number of line items.
  • Typing a style number pulls the garment straight out of BT Catalog — description, colours and its real size run — or you can type anything in by hand.
  • Upload each logo, name it, then pick that name per line item so we know which art goes where.
  • Orders list and a full order page with live status and a history trail.
  • Shop side: an Orders queue under BT Accounts to review a submission, move its status, and link it to a BT Portal job card — after which status follows the card automatically.
  • Statuses are BT Portal's job-card statuses, shown to the customer in plainer wording.

0.3.0

  • Every BT plugin now shows the same Updates section in the same place — last on the page, same heading, same button, same wording. Shared file, so they cannot drift apart again.
  • Version info moved out of Status into the shared Updates section at the bottom, where it is on every other BT plugin.

0.2.2

  • Added the Status panel and Check for updates button that every other BT plugin has — installed vs published version, with a link straight to Plugins.
  • The panel also self-tests the parts that fail silently: database tables present, the /accounts URL actually routed, and BT Quote available for pricing. A broken deploy now shows here instead of when someone tries to sign in.
  • A missing /accounts route links straight to Settings → Permalinks with the fix.

0.2.1

  • BT Accounts now sits with the other BT plugins in the admin sidebar instead of drifting up beside Analytics.
  • Registers itself with BT Quote's grouping via the new bt_menu_group_order filter, and falls back to a menu position beside BT Quote if that grouping is unavailable.

0.2.0

  • Portal restyled on Boomer T's branding — navy #27267e, magenta accents, Oswald headings and Tahoma body, matching the Quick Quote tool.
  • Sign-in page rebuilt: navy gradient, branded header card, magenta sign-in button.
  • Portal header now leads with Boomer T's and shows the account's logo in a chip edged with their brand colour.
  • Optional Boomer T's logo setting (BT Accounts → Portal branding); falls back to the Oswald wordmark.
  • Footer pinned to the bottom on short pages.

0.1.0

  • Phase 1 skeleton: contract account portal at /accounts.
  • Portal logins are self-contained — not WordPress users, no wp-admin access, no capabilities anywhere in WordPress.
  • Accounts admin screen: branding, PO requirement, garment-purchase flag, per-account logins.
  • Per-account pricing rides BT Quote's existing btq_pricing_tables filter, so the engine is not forked and the public quoter is unaffected.
  • Login throttling, hashed sessions, per-session CSRF tokens, nocache headers on every portal response.
